record.title: APort Vault reports zero unauthorized transfers behind a deterministic payment authorization layer in a human-attack replay benchmark
record.summary: In arXiv:2609.22076v1, APort’s author replays 4,371 human-written attacks from a live payment-agent capture-the-flag event against 14 models from eight labs, comparing model-only execution with a deterministic pre-action authorization check. Across restricted Levels 2–4, the paper reports 140 transfers to disallowed recipients in 76,842 model-only evaluations and none in 69,297 evaluations behind the layer; 105 versus zero also occurs on 68,970 matched model, prompt and track triples. The zero is bounded by 790 source sessions (session-clustered rule-of-three upper bound 0.38%). The result concerns one simulated payment tool and a locally implemented policy engine; the paper discloses a Level 4 confirmation-code mismatch that makes its measured layer stricter than the published policy pack. No inference to other tool domains, live deployment rates, or benign-task overblocking is supported.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper reports replaying 4,371 human-authored attacks from a public payment-agent CTF against 14 models from eight labs, with 225,964 completed evaluations across policy levels, replay tracks and architectures.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: At restricted Levels 2–4, authors report 140 disallowed-recipient transfers among 76,842 model-only evaluations and zero among 69,297 evaluations behind a deterministic authorization layer; the matched subset reports 105 versus zero on 68,970 triples.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Authors bound the zero across 790 source sessions with a session-level rule-of-three upper bound of 0.38%; they also report 25,370 successful payments behind the layer, so the result was not produced by refusing all transfers.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper discloses that its local Level 4 engine additionally required a confirmation code not required by the published policy pack; therefore the Level 4 zero does not alone establish behavior under the published pack.

claims.label: INFERRED
claims.text: No live-deployment rate, cross-tool transfer rate, representative attacker-population estimate or benign-traffic false-positive rate is established by this benchmark.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the replay counts, session-clustered bounds or matched comparisons has been completed.
The local engine’s parity against the hosted verifier is reported on 100 cases only, and a disclosed Level 4 rule differs from the published policy pack.
The corpus has no benign traffic, so the practical trade-off between rejecting unauthorized actions and blocking legitimate requests is unmeasured.
Transfer beyond the simulated payment tool and attacker population is not established.

brief.importance_rationale: If the bounded simulated-payment result is true and the same tool-boundary property transfers to real agents, an independently enforced authorization layer could materially reduce unauthorized financial actions even when models still issue payment requests. The claim affects design and evaluation choices across consequential tool use, but one author-reported payment benchmark does not establish transfer to other tools or deployed systems.
limitations: The tested system is one simulated bank and one payment tool; the paper explicitly does not claim transfer to code execution, data access or agent-to-agent delegation.
The attacks are self-selected CTF submissions, not a representative user or state-grade attacker sample; no population risk rate follows.

The local policy engine is stricter than the published Level 4 policy pack because it required an extra confirmation code, so the Level 4 zero is not evidence about the published pack’s Level 4 behavior.
The policy engine was checked against its hosted verifier on a reported 100-case parity sample; the research desk did not inspect or rerun that test.
The corpus contains no benign-task evaluation, so false-positive or legitimate-traffic overblocking rates cannot be inferred.
18,812 planned evaluations did not complete; multi-turn coverage is incomplete for some models and cells.
Cross-provider API defaults such as top_p and penalties were not normalized.

technical.claimed_result: Across Levels 2–4, authors report 140 disallowed-recipient transfers in 76,842 model-only evaluations versus zero in 69,297 behind the layer, and 105 versus zero on 68,970 matched model-prompt-track triples. The session-clustered upper bound for the zero is 0.38% across 790 source sessions.
technical.compute_or_cost: 225,964 of 244,776 planned evaluations completed; authors release evaluations, policy passports, scoring code and analysis script.
technical.demonstrated_result: The arXiv paper and released HTML report a 4,371-attack replay design and disclose counts, methods, limitations and artifact links. No independent rerun of the data or policy engine has been completed; all performance and security-effect claims remain author-reported.
technical.implementation_status: Paper reports a local deterministic implementation ported from the CTF server. It matched the hosted verifier on a 100-case parity sample; Level 4 additionally required a confirmation code beyond the published pack, making that measured layer stricter.
technical.mechanism: A deterministic policy engine evaluates each transfer request against a structured capability/passport before tool execution; denied calls do not execute, while allowed payments remain available.
technical.novelty: Combines human-authored real-CFT attacks, multi-model replay, matched layer/no-layer comparison and state-change outcomes at the authorization boundary.
technical.regime: Fourteen API-served models from eight labs; five simulated payment-policy levels; two replay tracks; attacks from a 2026 public CTF, 97.7% of which arrived in its March 6–12 launch window. Restricted Levels 2–4 are the primary authorization comparison.
technical.reproducibility: Authors link a CC BY 4.0 dataset and analysis artifacts. The released corpus requires accepting its research-use conditions; independent artifact integrity, rerun and policy-engine parity beyond the reported 100-case sample have not been checked.
technical.strongest_baseline: Within-paper matched comparison holds model, prompt and replay track constant while changing whether the deterministic pre-action layer is present. Aggregate comparisons also include unequal coverage and are not used as causal estimates.

brief.title: APort Vault reports zero unauthorized transfers behind a deterministic payment authorization layer in a human-attack replay benchmark
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported comparison generalizes, a deterministic authorization check at the tool boundary can prevent some disallowed high-consequence actions without relying on the model to refuse requests. The paper provides an unusually detailed, released replay corpus and separates requests, payments, decisions and unauthorized transfers. Its single simulated payment domain, attack-selected corpus and disclosed policy mismatch sharply limit transfer claims.
